answer.answer: kg keeps the cache outside the store, in the user's cache directory: $XDG_CACHE_HOME/kg/validated/ (by default ~/.cache/kg/validated/). After a write or a successful load it leaves an empty marker file there. The marker is named after a SHA-256 hash of kg's version, the JSON schema (serialized with sorted keys) and the raw bytes of graph.json. If a later read finds a marker for those contents, it skips schema validation. Any change to graph.json, or a different kg version or schema, gives a new hash, so the store is validated in full again. Only the latest 256 markers are kept. If the cache cannot be written, every read validates. This was added in commit 7947ba7 (perf(store), #67, RNF-06).

(1) The v0.2 benchmark on four small repos (4-104 files; 6 pilot + 17 main questions, #39) found the graph tied with reading the code: code 1.00, graph alone 0.98, graph-guided reading 1.00. It was not cheaper overall, though it took fewer calls on 6 of 7 multi-hop questions, and compact node cards (#52) cut context to 4,411 vs 11,974 chars at the same score. (2) The stale-graph runs showed a stale graph is safe but not useful: the agent always reported staleness and never overclaimed, but scored 0.63 vs 1.00 for code (0.83 once it could read the files kg status flagged, at 3-4x the context). (3) The first experiment of v0.3, the large-repo run on scrapy (489 files, 16 questions, #52), showed reading the code won: code 0.99/29 s vs cards 0.98/92 s, hybrid 0.97, graph 0.93/115 s. Part of the slowness was kg re-validating its 11.5 MB store on every query, and accuracy was lost on facts the graph lacks (TYPE_CHECKING imports, inheritance, settings/string-loaded classes). (4) The redesign step 0 (#67) made kg's reads about 6x faster (4.9 s to 0.8 s) and gave the agent the graph next to search ('companion'), with a lean control. Companion scored 0.96 vs 0.98 for code and 0.99 for lean, and used less context (5,199 vs 8,731 chars). It failed the pre-set gate on time (+45%, limit was +30%). The lean control showed that on questions where kg was not called, the saving came from a prompt line, not the graph. Where the graph was used it cut reading by 56% at the same score but cost 35% more time, and on the scrapy/utils/job.py impact question it scored 0.50 (kg impact listed 261 modules vs 11). Following the plan's own rule, kg stopped being developed as a code-graph tool for agents: the graph never made an answer more accurate.
